<gmane_tag_quotation_marker> <gmane_tag_quotation> Well, that doesn't seem correct.  The Germans *are* the Scenario Attacker

E1.41 If a side is designated by SSR as the Scenario Attacker, can Cloaking
still be used even if all his forces set up on board?
A. Yes. [An97; Mw]

E1.411 vaguely implies the opposite but it is a particularly poorly-written
rule (a strong effort given how little it actually says).  Given the above
Q&A, it should be reworded to effectively delete the first sentence --
offboard setup is not required for a *designated* Scenario Attacker.

Keep in mind that there are only two ways for a side to be classed as
"Scenario Attacker" (or "Defender"): either it fulfils the criteria
established in the Index, or an SSR specifies it.  Regardless, per the Index
definition, you cannot have one without the other.

It seems as though that Perry believes the SSR for PB2 is to give the British
the advantages (but not the disadvantages) of being Scenario Defender.  If so
it should have been worded differently if the intent was also to prevent the
Germans from getting the advantages of being Scenario Attacker.  (Note that if
SSR 2 hadn't mentioned that the British are Scenario Defender, neither side
would be, because they don't fulfil the Index criteria.)
